title: Submit Replication or Reproduction Study to FLoRA
description:
Please use this form if you would like to submit a reproduction or replication study in a brief and semi-structured format.
When can a study be considered to be a reproduction?
The study is assigned to one original study that tested at least one same hypothesis.
The study uses the same dataset as the original study.
When can a study be considered to be a replication?
The study is assigned to one original study that tested at least one same hypothesis.
The study tries to mirror the methods of the original study and justify deviations
Replicated and reported tests use data that differ from the data used in the original study.

Is this form for references, studies, or findings?
In this form, we ask you to enter references that include at least one replication or reproduction. You can indicate how many studies are included in the reference. Specifically, we are looking for unique pairs of 'original study + replication study'.

Will I become a contributor to the FORRT Library of Reproduction and Replication Attempts (FLoRA) by using this form?
You need to submit at least five new and correct entries via this form and write an email to lukas.roeseler@uni-muenster.de if you would like to be listed as a contributor to the FORRT Replication Database.

How long does it take for my entry to be added to the FORRT Replication Database?
As of spring 2026, the database is undergoing major expansion. Time for addition may range from one week to multiple months. Please send us an email if you want to learn about the status of your submission.

Type of Replication Reference (must be a complete and citable study, i.e., no preregistration, no email exchange, no published data without report; if there are multiple replication studies of the same target study in a paper, please try to code what the authors say about each individual study with one filled-out form per study)
options: Individual Study (i.e., one paper with one study)
Multiple Studies (i.e., one paper with multiple studies)
Results only (i.e., there is no paper with a thorough description of the study)

items.title: Meta Paper: For a replication reference that includes multiple studies: Are all studies on the same topic or does it include unrelated replications/reproductions (e.g., Open Science Collaboration, 2015 includes many unrelated studies). For example, a paper reporting replications of two different original papers would not be considered a meta paper.
options: All studies are on the same topic
Studies are not all on the same topic

items.title: Description (e.g., "cascade effect (eye tracking) ", "red romance effect", "people are more sensitive to the dosage of harm-based transgressions than purity transgressions")
Reference - Original in APA format with DOI

Reference - Replication in APA format with DOI
If your submission is referring to a study included in a meta-paper that is not also published as a stand-alone report (e.g., Open Science Collaboration, 2015), please paste here the reference to the meta-paper.

Report URL - Replication
If your submission is referring to a study included in a meta-paper OR if your reference has not been assigned a DOI please put here the (stable) URL to the individual report.
Replication outcome as reported by the replication authors (please select)
options: Uninformative (should is coded if the replication authors explicitly say so, e.g., because their sample was too small)

Statistically successful but flawed (refers to replications where that is the main message [e.g., “we replicated x using the original methods, but show that they are not a valid test of the hypotheses”])
Descriptive / not applicable (when consistency with original is not of interest, e.g. for some qualitative replications)
